STANDARD FORM OF CONTRACT 
FOR 
RAILWAY OPERATION & MAINTENANCE  
 
 
PWD Railway Operation & Maintenance Form (2024) 
Hak Cipta Terpelihara Kerajaan Malaysia 
This form has been approved by the Attorney General’s Chamber

RAILWAY OPERATION & MAINTENANCE SERVICES

RECITALS 
A. The Government requires safe, reliable, and e]icient operation and maintenance 
services for the railway infrastructure and operations; B. The Contractor agrees to provide 
such O&M Services, and has the relevant skills, experience, and competence to do so 
under this Contract. 
 
1. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION 
1.1 Definitions 
For this Contract, unless the context otherwise requires, the following apply:  
“Authority” means any statutory, government or regulatory body or agency which must 
provide its consent or approval for the provision of Railway O&M Services;  
“Commencement Date” means the date determined as the start of the Railway O&M 
Services as set out in Clause 2.1;  
“Contract” means this legally binding agreement, including its appendices and any 
amendments made in writing;  
“Contract Documents” refers to this contract and all documents listed in the List of 
Appendices;  
“Contract Expiry Date” means the date the Contract Period ends as given in Clause 2.1;  
“Contract Period” means the period for which this Contract remains in force, as referred 
to in Clause 2.1;  
“Contract Sum” means the total value contracted for Railway O&M Services as set out in 
Clause 4;  
“Existing Rail Management Information System” means a computerized system or 
manual process already in use when the contract commences, for tracking rail operation, 
maintenance, and performance;  
“Railway Operation & Maintenance Services” or "O&M Services" means all those works, 
services and deliverables specified in Appendix 10 and further described in the O&M 
Technical Specifications in Appendix 7A;  

“Railway Operations Manager” means the person, fully qualified and experienced, 
appointed by the Contractor to administer and deliver the Railway O&M Services;  
“Railway Superintending Oeicer” ("RSO") means the o]icer so designated by the 
Government under Clause 23 to oversee the Contractor's performance;  
“RSO’s Representative” means any individual delegated and authorized in writing by the 
RSO to act on his/her behalf as permitted by this contract;  
“Government’s Intellectual Property” means all technical data, documentation, 
software, drawings, plans, or other materials owned or provided by the Government;  
“Management Information System” means any Contractor-developed or maintained 
system for managing asset inventory, operations, or maintenance records and reporting;  
“Performance Requirement” means the minimum obligations and key performance 
indicators laid out in Appendix 7B;  
“Provisional Sum” means a sum set aside for specific O&M Services as may be directed 
by the Government per Clause 30.3;  
“Site” means all railway lines, stations, depots, yards, signal rooms and control centers, 
as identified in Appendix 8;  
“Site Oeice” means the Contractor's administration point or premises located at the Site;  
“Working Day” means a day other than a public holiday, Saturday, or Sunday, as 
recognized by Malaysian law in the place the O&M Services are performed. 
 
1.2 Interpretation 
Unless inconsistent with the context: (a) Singular includes the plural and vice versa; (b) The 
masculine includes the feminine and vice versa; (c) Reference to any person includes a 
company, statutory body, partnership; (d) References to clauses, appendices etc. refer to 
those in this contract; (e) References to parties include their successors and permitted 
assigns; (f) Payments by the Government will be made in Malaysian Ringgit, by cheque or 
bank transfer to Contractor’s account; (g) References to laws include all 
1.3 Notices, Consents, and Approvals 
All communications (notices, consents, approvals, certificates, determinations) required 
under this Contract must be in writing, unless expressly stated otherwise. 
1.4 Time Period 

Any date or period for the performance of any act under this contract includes any variation 
to that period as agreed in writing by the parties. 
1.5 Resolution of Ambiguities and Discrepancies 
If the Contractor finds any discrepancy, ambiguity, or inconsistency in the Contract 
Documents, it must immediately notify the RSO in writing. The RSO will issue instructions 
to resolve such discrepancy, and the Contractor will comply accordingly. Any additional 
costs due to such resolutions fall upon the Contractor unless otherwise stated. 
 
2. CONTRACT PERIOD 
2.1 Contract Period 
This Contract is valid for ____ years commencing from __________ (the “Commencement 
Date”) and will expire on __________ (the “Contract Expiry Date”), unless terminated earlier 
in accordance with this Contract. 
2.2 Consequences of Expiry 
Upon expiry of the Contract Period: (a) The Contractor shall: (i) Cease performing O&M 
Services; (ii) Vacate all Sites and remove equipment within fourteen (14) days; (iii) Fully 
cooperate for a smooth handover of services, sta], and information to the Government or 
its appointee; (iv) Return all Government-owned property, records, and documents; (v) 
Handover all Operations Management data and systems in working order. (b) The 
Government shall pay all monies due up to the expiry date, subject to set-o]s permitted by 
this Contract. 
 
3. SCOPE OF RAILWAY OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE SERVICES 
3.1 The Contractor shall perform all Railway O&M Services described in Appendix 10 
and achieve all standards and obligations imposed in this Contract and as required in 
Appendix 7B. 
3.2 The RSO may require additional services, outside the primary scope, to be 
performed in accordance with the variation procedures in Clause 29. 
 
 
 

 
4. CONTRACT SUM 
4.1 In consideration for the services, the Government shall pay the Contractor the sum 
of 
Ringgit: ____________________________ (RM____) (the “Contract Sum”). 
4.2 The Contract Sum is fixed except for permitted variations specifically approved 
pursuant to this Contract. 
 
5. TERMS OF PAYMENT 
5.1 The Government shall pay the Contractor monthly at amounts reflecting actual 
and proper performance, as certified by the RSO. 
5.2 Each monthly payment application must include: 
(a) Value of O&M Services executed in the month (refer Appendix 4); (b) Payments for 
approved variations; (c) Provisional sum expenditure with documentation; (d) Required 
reports and records specified in Appendix 7A and 7B; (e) Supporting evidence (logs, site 
diaries, service reports, invoices, delivery orders, and as-built drawings as required); 
5.3 If Contractor does not submit necessary reports, the RSO will value the work 
based on available documents only. 
5.4 The RSO will certify payment within fourteen (14) days of a satisfactory application. 
5.5 The Government shall pay within thirty (30) days of certification. 
 
6. PERFORMANCE BOND 
6.1 The Contractor shall provide an irrevocable Performance Bond in favour of the 
Government, equal to five percent (5%) of the Contract Sum, from a licensed 
Malaysian financial institution, valid until twelve (12) months after the Contract Expiry 
Date. 
6.2 If any part of the Performance Bond is called, the Contractor must immediately 
reinstate it to the full value. 
6.3 Should the Contractor fail to perform, the Government may forfeit the 
Performance Bond proportional to the underperformance or loss. 

 
7. OBLIGATIONS OF THE CONTRACTOR 
During the Contract Period, the Contractor shall: (a) Provide all Railway O&M Services to 
the standards and schedule required; (b) Submit and follow an O&M Plan acceptable to the 
Government; (c) Ensure all work is carried out with care, skill, and in accordance with best 
industry practice; (d) Protect the Government’s assets and legal interests at all times; (e) 
Use best e]orts to prevent abuse, damage, or waste; (f) Employ and maintain skilled, 
qualified, and experienced personnel in su]icient numbers; (g) Maintain all records, 
documentation, and reporting systems as required; (h) Inform Government promptly, in 
writing, of any event likely to a]ect O&M Services; (i) Promptly notify and provide 
recommendations in the case of any accident, breakdown, or emergency; (j) At its own 
cost, provide and maintain, in adequate working order, all equipment, vehicles, and tools 
necessary for Railway O&M; (k) Supervise, manage, and train its sta] as required for the 
safe and e]icient delivery of all services. 
 
8. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF THE CONTRACTOR 
8.1 As of the Commencement Date, the Contractor warrants and represents: 
(a) It is a company validly registered under the laws of Malaysia; (b) It has all approvals and 
authorizations to enter into and perform this contract; (c) This contract constitutes a 
binding legal agreement; (d) Its execution of the contract does not breach any laws, rules, 
or corporate obligations; (e) There are no legal proceedings pending which would materially 
a]ect its ability to perform; (f) No illegal or corrupt practices were used to secure the award 
of this contract; (g) It has the financial and technical capacity to perform all obligations. 
8.2 These warranties continue for the entire Contract Period. 
 
9. RAILWAY OPERATING PLAN 
9.1 The Contractor shall, within fourteen (14) days of the Commencement Date, 
submit its Railway Operating and Maintenance Plan (the “O&M Plan”) to the RSO for 
approval. 
9.2 The RSO will approve, reject, or request clarification or revision within fourteen (14) 
days. If not acted upon, the O&M Plan will be deemed accepted. 

9.3 The Contractor must comply with all duties and transition provisions in the 
approved O&M Plan. 
9.4 The Contractor must amend the O&M Plan promptly when directed by the RSO, to 
account for performance issues or operational changes. 
 
10. INSPECTION OF RAILWAY SITES 
10.1 The Contractor is deemed to have fully inspected all Sites and appraised itself of 
all operational and site conditions before signing this contract. 
10.2 Information supplied by the Government does not relieve the Contractor of its 
duties and due diligence. 
 
11. OPERATIONS REQUIREMENTS AND PERFORMANCE 
11.1 The Contractor shall maintain all facilities, equipment, tracks, rolling stock, 
stations, and systems to the standards prescribed in Appendix 7B. 
11.2 The Contractor must submit all operational and maintenance reports required by 
Appendix 7A, at the required frequency, for both payment and performance review. 
11.3 If the Contractor fails to meet performance indicators, the Government is entitled 
to deduct, from any payment, penalties calculated as defined in Appendix 7B. 
Deductions may also be made against the Performance Bond. 
 
12. RAILWAY OPERATIONS MANAGER 
12.1 The Contractor must appoint a suitably skilled and qualified Railway Operations 
Manager, who shall always be present at the Site and fluent in both Bahasa Malaysia 
and English. 
12.2 Upon Government’s request, any unsuitable Operations Manager must be 
replaced immediately at the Contractor’s cost. 
 
13. EMPLOYMENT OF WORKERS 
13.1 All workers must be skilled, trained, and qualified for railway operation and 
safety, and must meet the requirements set in Appendix 7A. 

LIST OF APPENDICES 
APPENDIX 1: FORM OF TENDER 
The o]icial tender submission document, as completed and submitted by the Contractor, 
duly signed and dated. 
APPENDIX 2: LETTER OF ACCEPTANCE OF TENDER 
A formal letter from the Government of Malaysia accepting the Contractor’s tender o]er, 
confirming contract award, start date, and initial terms. 
APPENDIX 3: SUMMARY OF TENDER 
A summary of key commercial o]ers, key personnel, service levels, technical approaches, 
and any clarifications or assumptions made as part of the Contractor’s tender submission. 
APPENDIX 4: SCHEDULE OF PRICE 
The full, itemized contract price schedule, including: 
• Routine Operation of Railway Lines 
• Maintenance of Rolling Stock 
• Maintenance of Track, Signalling, and Electrification 
• Depot Services 
• Emergency Response 
• Supply of Materials and Spares 
• Any variable or provisional rate items 
• Grand total contract sum 
APPENDIX 5: APPENDIX TO THE CONDITIONS OF CONTRACT 
Essential project-specific information, including, but not limited to: 
• Names and posts of all Government o]icers authorized to issue instructions 
(including Railway Superintending O]icer, etc.) 
• Details of financial limits and authority for variations 
• Performance bond amount 

• Statutory insurance requirements (sum insured, periods of insurance, policy 
numbers, amount of excess, etc.) 
• On-cost charges percentages 
APPENDIX 6: TREASURY’S INSTRUCTIONS 
Authoritative Treasury Instructions or guidelines that are applicable to this contract, 
including procurement, payment, import/export, audit, or financial management. 
APPENDIX 7: GOVERNMENT’S REQUIREMENT 
Any overarching technical, safety, operational or policy requirement stipulated by the 
Government for all contractors, including access, security, and environmental policies. 
APPENDIX 7A: RAILWAY OPERATION & MAINTENANCE TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS 
Detailed, discipline-by-discipline specifications for all O&M activities, for example: 
• Railway operating procedures 
• Scheduled and preventive maintenance plans 
• Emergency and breakdown procedures 
• Technical standards for inspection of tracks, rolling stock, electrical and signalling 
equipment 
• Required certifications for sta] and materials 
• Maintenance frequencies and methods 
APPENDIX 7B: PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS 
Service Level Agreements (SLAs), performance indicators, minimum availability and 
reliability metrics for all railway assets and services, including: 
• Train punctuality and service reliability targets 
• Rolling stock and track availability 
• Maintenance response and rectification timeframes 
• Penalty and deduction mechanisms tied to performance failure 
APPENDIX 8: SITE INFORMATION AND ASSET INVENTORIES 
Comprehensive register of all physical assets to be operated and/or maintained, to include: 

• Site and railway route plans 
• Lists of stations, depots, yards, and other railway facilities 
• Rolling stock inventory (numbers, types, ages, serial numbers) 
• Signalling, communications, power equipment inventories 
• Condition assessments, if available 
APPENDIX 9: FORM OF GUARANTEE FOR PERFORMANCE BOND 
Standard template for the bank/insurer's guarantee in favor of the Government, indicating 
the surety’s obligations and claiming details. 
APPENDIX 10: SCOPE OF RAILWAY OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE SERVICES 
A detailed breakdown, narrative, and/or matrix fully describing the Contractor’s scope, 
mapped to technical, safety, and service standards set by the Government. To include but 
not be limited to: 
• Daily, weekly, and preventive operational and maintenance routines 
• Breakdown and emergency coverage 
• Technical, administrative, and compliance obligations 
• Interfaces with Government or third parties (e.g., railway police, ticketing, asset 
management, etc.)
